---
title: "The recode"
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
```

One rule governs this chapter: **every derived variable is created in `R/01_recode.R`,
and nowhere else.** Analysis scripts read the result; they never recode. The rule exists
because an agent asked to "add a measure" will otherwise add it wherever it is currently
looking, and two months later two scripts disagree about what `party3` means.

## The script

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| class-output: sourceCode
cat(readLines("R/01_recode.R"), sep = "\n")
```

## Running it

```{r}
source("R/01_recode.R")
wss <- read_rds("data/wss_clean.rds")
dim(wss)
```

It writes `data/wss_clean.rds`, which is git-ignored: the artifact is cheap to rebuild
and the script is the thing worth versioning.

## What each line produced

```{r}
wss |> count(auth_group)
```

```{r}
wss |> count(age_group)
```

```{r}
wss |> count(party3)
```

```{r}
wss |> count(latino, year)
```

`authoritarianism` is the row mean of the four items, so it is bounded 0–1 by
construction — and worth checking rather than assuming:

```{r}
summary(wss$authoritarianism)
```

::: {.warn}
[`rowMeans(..., na.rm = TRUE)` is a decision, not a default]{.warn-head}
A respondent who answered one of four items gets a score built from that one item. That
may be what you want, or it may not; either way it is an imputation rule, and it should
be a deliberate choice rather than an argument an agent supplied because it suppresses
`NA`s. A stricter version requires a minimum number of items:

```r
auth_n = rowSums(!is.na(pick(auth1:auth4))),
authoritarianism = if_else(auth_n >= 3,
                           rowMeans(pick(auth1:auth4), na.rm = TRUE),
                           NA_real_)
```
:::

## How much did the recode cost us?

Derived variables inherit missingness from their inputs. Always know how much:

```{r}
wss |>
  summarise(across(c(authoritarianism, auth_group, age_group, party3, latino),
                   ~ sum(is.na(.x)))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "variable", values_to = "n_miss") |>
  mutate(pct = round(100 * n_miss / nrow(wss), 1)) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

## Asking an agent to extend it

A usable prompt is narrow, names its file, and asks for evidence:

```text
Read AGENTS.md and R/01_recode.R. Add an income-tercile variable built from
faminc, weighted by `weight`. Add it to R/01_recode.R only. Then show me
the diff and a count() of the new variable.
```

Then check three things before you keep it: that the cutpoints are what you'd have
chosen, that `faminc` really runs 1–16 with no missing-data codes hiding inside that
range (the codebook, not `range()`, settles this), and that the row count of
`wss_clean.rds` has not changed. [The next chapter](08-analysis.qmd) uses these
variables; [the one after](09-tests.qmd) makes the checks permanent.
